units.translation: a tearful hope of saving seed.
do not wipe out this seed of the Pelopids.
the great seed of a revered mother.
the seed of a cow with fine offspring.
Megareus, seed of Creon.
and you, seed of Anachaeus.
Spercheus
Spercheus, a river of Thessaly.
where Spercheus waters the plain with kindly drink.
O river Spercheus.
hasty, swift
hasty, swift. Explained by Hesychius as ταχὺς [swift], ἐπειγόμενος [hurrying], σπουδαῖος [eager], ἄγαν ἐγκείμενος πρός τι [pressing hard upon something].
hasty messengers.
swift, hurrying, eager, pressing hard upon something
to hasten, to be eager, to press on with something
to hasten, to be eager, to press on with something.
Middle form σπεύδομαι [I hasten].
he will come to me for reconciliation and friendship, hastening to one who hastens.
whenever someone himself hastens.
hastening, so that Zeus might never rule over the gods.
and how I may best hasten to receive my revered husband when he returns.
the mind bears some haste of counsel.
hastening another sacrifice.
hastening (thus Burges for σπευδόμεναι [hastening]) to remove someone (Pauw: Zeus) from these cares.
I hasten
spread out, ample, long
spread out, ample, long. Explained by grammarians cited in Thes. vol. 7 p. 591 as μέγας [great], πλατὺς [broad], εὐρὺς [wide], μακρός [long].
a long stretch of road.
great, broad, wide, long
viscus
viscus. Of the lung.
Of the womb.
More frequently in the plural σπλάγχνα [viscera].
Of the heart or the midriff.
Similarly Pindar and Sophocles used the plural: see Thes. vol. 7 p. 600.
with many man-wearing toils the lung pants.
terrible is the common womb from which we were born, of a wretched mother and an unhappy father.
and the smoothness of the viscera.
with entrails and viscera – having them as is fitting.
the heart, moving in a circle, does not idle in the viscera.
my viscera grow dark as I hear the word.
bloody whetstones, harms to young viscera.

to strike, to beat, to smite.

ashes
ashes. Of the ashes of a dead person.
instead of men, urns and ashes arrive at each man's house.
a tearful grain of ash that was once a man.
and the ash, dying with him, sends forth rich breaths of wealth.
the sides of the bronze cauldron hide the ash of the man.
libation
libation.
σπονδαὶ χαλίκρητοι [libations mixed with pure wine] he cites from Aeschylus, who seems to have had in mind χαλίκρητον μέθυ [wine mixed with pure water], which is Archilochus's in Athen. 1 p. 8 a.
the Argives must pray and sacrifice and pour libations as to the Olympian gods.
freshly mixed libations.

indeed from this sowing a bold man will be born.
crop
crop.
the crop rejoices in the Zeus-given brightness in the birth-pangs of the bud.
haste, speed
haste, speed.
where I conjectured σπουδὴ δὲ καὶ τοῦ συγκαταρτίζει πόδα [and haste also to join the foot].
Very often it is used in the sense of zeal or effort. In a spurious verse: πατρίς τε γαῖα σῆς ὑπὸ σπουδῆς δορὶ ἁλοῦσα [and the fatherland, taken by the spear through your zeal].
